questions.q: n-Butylamine (I), diethylamine (II) and N,N-dimethylethyl amine (III) have the same molar mass. The increasing order of their boiling point is
questions.solution:
$\mathop{{H}_{3}C - C{H}_{2} - C{H}_{2} - C{H}_{2} - N{H}_{2}}_{\text{n-butylamine}\left(\text{primary amine}\right)}$

$\mathop{C{H}_{3}C{H}_{2} - NH - C{H}_{2} - C{H}_{3}}_{\text{Diethylamine}\left(\text{Secondary amine}\right)}$

$\mathop{C{H}_{3} - \overset{C{H}_{3}}{\overset{|}{N} - {C}_{2}{H}_{5}}}_{\text{ethyldimethylamine} ( \text{tertiary amine} )}$

Primary amines have two hydrogen atoms available for hydrogen bond formation, while $2 °$ amines have only one hydrogen atom for hydrogen bond formation. $3 °$ amines do not have intermolecular association due to absence of hydrogen atom.

Thus, order of boiling point of isomeric amines is as follows

$3 ° < 2 ° < 1 °$

or $III < II < I$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Arrange the following anilines in decreasing order of basicity

$1.{C}_{6}{H}_{5}N{H}_{2}$

$2.o - C{H}_{3}{C}_{6}{H}_{4}N{H}_{2}$

$3.m - C{H}_{3}{C}_{6}{H}_{4}N{H}_{2}$

$4.p - C{H}_{3}{C}_{6}{H}_{4}N{H}_{2}$
questions.solution:
$- C{H}_{3}$ group is inductively electron-donating and base-strengthening from all position. Moreover, if $- C{H}_{3}$ is attached to benzene ring (or if R has benzylic H), it is electron-donating by hyper-conjugation from the ortho and para positions. Because of ortho effect, o-substituted aniline become less basic than aniline. Thus,

$p - C{H}_{3}{C}_{6}{H}_{4}N{H}_{2}$ (hyper-conjugation and induction) > $m - C{H}_{3}{C}_{6}{H}_{4}N{H}_{2}$ (induction) > ${C}_{6}{H}_{5}N{H}_{2} > o - C{H}_{3}{C}_{6}{H}_{4}N{H}_{2}$ (ortho effect).

${C}_{6}{H}_{5}N{H}_{2}\overset{NaN{O}_{2} + HCl}{\to}X\overset{C{u}_{2} ( CN{)}_{2}}{\to}Y\overset{{H}_{2}O / {H}^{+}}{\to}Z\overset{NaOH / CaO, \Delta}{\to}P\overset{C{l}_{2}, hν\left(Excess\right)}{\to}Q$
questions.solution:
${C}_{6}{H}_{5}N{H}_{2}\overset{NaN{O}_{2} / HCl}{\to}{C}_{6}{H}_{5}{N}_{2}^{+}Cl\overset{C{u}_{2} ( CN{)}_{2}}{\to}{C}_{6}{H}_{5}CN\overset{{H}_{2}O / {H}^{+}}{\to}{C}_{6}{H}_{5}COOH$

${C}_{6}{H}_{5}COOH\overset{NaOH / CaO, \Delta}{\to}{C}_{6}{H}_{6}\overset{C{l}_{2}, hν ( Excess )}{\to}{C}_{6}{H}_{6}C{l}_{6}$

It is diazotisation reaction to produce X, then sandmayer's reaction to give Y, followed by hydrolysis to produce benzoic acid (Z). Benzoic acid on decarboxylation gives benzene, which on excess photochlorination gives benzene hexa chloride.
